candidate.representation: Facetwise controlled exponential generator H_i(x,k;theta_i), maximized over the measured coupled resource polytope K(x), with exact falling-factorial error D_i and stopped exponential potential.
candidate.hypothesis: Preserving coupling may certify finite-volume safety when an independent reaction-rate box does not. The toy verifies that logical separation, but no new scientific theorem/application advantage is claimed beyond a conditional refinement of N35.

missing_lemma: A reviewed, efficient data-to-certificate method that constructs K(x), Q and strict coupled collars from noisy enzyme/proteome/flux measurements with quantified uncertainty and practical complexity; also a nontrivial biological network showing material improvement over equally informed controls.
comparator: Replace K={(q,q):q in [1,16]} by the independent box [1,16]^2. It admits x=1/4,(k_A,k_B)=(16,1), with left-facet drift -7/16, so the inward-collar certificate fails. For small finite-volume networks, compare the certificate with the exact finite-state Bellman/CTMDP reachability ODE using the same K and information.
falsifier_or_next_experiment: Algebraic rejection by a feasible collar pair with H_i>-eta_i, exact CTMC risk exceeding the bound, or invalid count/pool/flux assumptions. Experimental test: log calibrated initial counts and volume, use measured enzyme/kcat and isotope flux polytope, then compare first-exit frequencies against the preregistered bound and matched equal-information CTMDP/box controls.
